LanguageData.DMS_BF_ExtendArmor.label: Additional Armor Plating
LanguageData.DMS_BF_ExtendArmor.description: Composite armor plates designed for battle frame pylons add survivability to the battle frame by protecting it from fragmentation and medium-caliber gunfire.
LanguageData.DMS_BF_ExtendCargo.label: Extended Cargo Rack
LanguageData.DMS_BF_ExtendCargo.description: A metal cargo box mounted on the battle frame's side pylons, commonly used for long-range transport in mountainous terrain and by frontline supply squads to improve hauling efficiency.
LanguageData.DMS_BF_RecoillessRifle.label: Recoilless Rifle Rack
LanguageData.DMS_BF_RecoillessRifle.description:
A pair of 65mm recoilless tubes mounted on the side pylons and tied into the frame's fire control chain, reloaded from the frame's carried stores between engagements.
The shaped-charge warhead punches through armor and fortification that the frame's own weapon cannot touch, though the jet goes into a single narrow channel and anything standing beside the point of impact walks away. The mass hanging on the pylons costs the frame walking pace, dodging room and cargo allowance.
LanguageData.DMS_CeramicsPlating.label: Ceramic Plates
LanguageData.DMS_CeramicsPlating.description: A disposable armor module whose array of ballistic ceramic plates effectively suppresses the kinetic and thermal erosion damage of bullets and shaped-charge jets, keeping the frame intact.\n\nExcellent protection, but strictly single-use: once damaged, a fresh plate has to be installed.
LanguageData.DMS_CommandCoprocessor.label: Command Coprocessor
LanguageData.DMS_CommandCoprocessor.description: An auxiliary processing board wired into the core processor. It offloads signal multiplexing and unit bookkeeping from the main processor, increasing the automatroid's control bandwidth at the cost of slightly higher energy consumption.
LanguageData.DMS_NuclearBattery.label: Nuclear Battery
LanguageData.DMS_NuclearBattery.description: A simple nuclear fission battery, common in unmanned signal stations and in mechs garrisoning beacons. Six near-critical columns of high-density uranium-235 are integrated with thermocouples and sealed inside a high-strength casing. Its output is enough to keep most models of mech running for hundreds of years, and in an emergency the unit itself can be turned into a one-shot nuclear bomb.
LanguageData.DMS_ReinforcedFrame.label: Reinforced Frame
LanguageData.DMS_ReinforcedFrame.description: A highly versatile internal structural reinforcement kit that replaces the wear-prone parts of a mech's skeleton with tungsteel alloy. It effectively improves durability in high-intensity combat and lets the mech keep moving unhindered under suppressing fire, at the cost of a significant increase in weight and a reduction in movement speed.
LanguageData.DMS_SyntheticTendon.label: Synthetic Tendon
LanguageData.DMS_SyntheticTendon.description: Artificial biosynthetic tendons installed at the load-bearing points of a mech's legs, drawing power from the mech's energy supply through an external interface. They effectively increase joint output, but also increase energy consumption.
LanguageData.DMS_TB_HeavyHydraulicFrame.label: Heavy Hydraulic Frame
LanguageData.DMS_TB_HeavyHydraulicFrame.description: An external hydraulic skeleton and power pack for heavy bipedal mechs - essentially an exoskeleton system built for mechs. It gives a heavy mech a much larger combat load capacity and allows superheavy weapons to be mounted, at the cost of a significant increase in weight and a reduction in movement speed.
